newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's SEPI unaware of Fenosa sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Spain's SEPI unaware of Fenosa sell-off.

text.p: The president of Spain's state industrial holding company SEPI said on Wednesday he did not know of any decision by public electricity company Endesa to sell its 7.5 percent share in Union Fenosa.
"I am not sure whether it will be sold or whether there has been a decision to sell", Pedro Ferreras told parliament's Industry Commission.
Talk that Endesa may sell its holding in Union Fenosa and take control of Fecsa and Sevillana by increasing its share participation has gathered strength in the press in recent days.

Ferreras said there had been no decision yet on whether Endesa would increase its share in Sevillana and Fesca from 39.4 percent and 49 percent respectively. The company's share in Union Fenosa was worth 118 billion pesetas, he added.
Such moves by Endesa would rock the consultation framework set up by the Industry Ministry to elaborate new electricity regulations in coming years, sector sources said.
